text:
maya: quick sync — bringing up titania-13b-quant with a two-stage speculative prefetch handoff. initial microbench looks promising but a small quality blip on long-context prompts.
eli: nice, what perf numbers do you have so far?
maya: baseline (no spec): p50=180ms, tps=230 toks/s. with spec-prefetch: p50=120ms, tps=420 toks/s (1.8x).
sanjay: huge. what's the quant config? q4 or q8 fallbacks?
maya: q4_0 weights, per-layer fallback to q8 for first 2 layers to avoid attention drift. packer uses 128-block tiling.
clara: which eval suites did you run? need to repro.
maya: ran codebench-small + convo-regressions + a 2k prompt long-form holdout. quick deltas: codebench accuracy 86 -> 83, convo-fluency automatic score stable, long-form coherence has more repetitions around token 600-900.
eli: repetition suggests stale KV or wrong prefetch ordering. can you paste the launch flags?
maya: sure:
```
MODEL=titania-13b-quant 
SERVE_ARGS="--spec-prefetch=handshake --handoff=two-stage --kv-cache=lazy --batch=auto --spec-timeout-ms=12" 
./deploy $MODEL $SERVE_ARGS
```
ops-bot: canary created: canary-1734567890-titania (3 nodes, 1% traffic).
eli: run an A/B with spec off and spec on and diff logits on the first 100 tokens; that isolates initial-token bias.
maya: started A/B. attaching quick diff (logit-cross-entropy):
- spec-on: avg_xent=1.12
- spec-off: avg_xent=1.08
so small reg, concentrated on tokens classified as entity spans.
sanjay: interesting. did you try increasing spec-timeout? maybe prefetch ordering racing with KV warmup.
maya: bumped to 20ms in a quick run: p50 increased to 135ms, tps dropped to 380, but xent gap shrank to 1.09 vs 1.08. tradeoff visible.
clara: we should run quality regressions against our eval harness with human-labeled prompts for the risky slice (entity-rich long-context). add a focused holdout set.
maya: agreed. I'll queue a full eval: 5k convo holdouts + 1k long entity prompts. also trying variant: q4_0 but disable per-layer fallback.
dev-bot: perf job queued: job-id=perf-1734567890-01.
ops-bot: rollback policy note: canary has auto-fallback to baseline if error-rate>2% or latency>300ms.
eli: also add a reproducible seed and capture KV indices at handoff time for a few traces. want to inspect attention keys in failing traces.
maya: doing that — will post traces and a short script to extract attention keys.
clara: if quality holds on the targeted holdout we can draft an ops runbook: recommended spec-timeout 12ms, fallback q8-first-2-layers, enable canary for 48h.
maya: prelim conclusion: spec-prefetch gives solid perf wins, small but measurable quality tradeoffs concentrated on long-context entity spans; tunable via timeout and quant fallback. next: full eval + attention trace inspection.
eli: thanks — ping when full eval done.
maya: will do. :thumbsup:
